Seasonable conditions are anticipated next week with additional chances for showers and thunderstorms as well as gradually decreasing temperatures.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
825 PM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 252 PM EDT Friday...

Increased confidence in rain next Thursday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 252 PM EDT Friday...

1. Intervals of scattered showers and thunderstorms with warm, 
humid conditions will continue through much of the weekend.

2. A brief period of lower humidity and dry conditions later 
Sunday into Monday morning will end with increasing chances of 
showers and thunderstorms later Monday. 

3. Seasonable conditions are anticipated next week with 
additional chances for showers and thunderstorms as well as 
gradually decreasing temperatures.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 252 PM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Isolated to scattered showers with a couple of 
thunderstorms remain on track for this evening into the overnight 
hours. For late this afternoon and evening, it appears our setup is 
reminiscent of yesterday with pulse storm potential. However, subtle 
differences will limit the thunderstorm threat. Instability over the 
Adirondack region is less robust, and so the ability for stronger 
convection will be limited by these initial weaker updrafts. 
However, increasing cyclonic flow as an upper level wave over the 
eastern Great Lakes gets slowly pushed towards our region will help 
generate more showers with time, peaking during the early morning 
hours and across northern portions of Vermont. With such weak 
forcing including lack of a well defined front or low pressure 
system, precipitation amounts will continue to be quite 
spatially variable. Activity will generally shift to the 
northeast with time, and pockets of heavier rainfall (~0.25 - 
0.5" with localized 1" amounts) will tend occur through tomorrow
morning. Some locations, probably in southern portions of 
Vermont, again should see little or no rain. 

For Saturday, there are again some mixed signals in terms of the 
convective evolution. Each of the last couple of cycles, machine 
learning guidance has been somewhat bullish on potential for some 
stronger thunderstorms. Consensus shows higher probabilities both 
south and east of our region; the latest Day 2 Storm Prediction 
Center severe risk does highlight the mid-Atlantic region again 
following today's stronger storms in that area as well. That being 
said, generally thunderstorm probabilities are roughly as high in 
our region as towards the south, with regionally greatest chances in 
northeastern Vermont and lowest chances in the southern St. Lawrence 
Valley and southern Vermont. Representative forecast soundings in 
St. Johnsbury during the early evening show MLCAPE of around 1500 
J/kg (moderately high CAPE) and effective shear of 10-15 knots (low 
wind shear), so the environment looks marginally supportive of pulse 
thunderstorms with mainly typical thunderstorms and a rare stronger 
wind gust possible. 

Following yesterday's anomalous moisture, precipitable water will be 
a bit lower tonight when it surges with the wave coming through 
(about 1.7" to 1.9"), and fall further tomorrow (about 1.5" to 
1.7"). So while a marginal (level 1 out of 5) risk of flash flooding 
continues associated with heavy rainfall rates in thunderstorms, 
think the footprints of 2" + that we saw yesterday are less likely. 
With meager instability available ahead of a final round 
of scattered showers moving through overnight Saturday into the 
day on Sunday, risk of impactful weather diminishes further as the 
weekend wears on. As the associated weak surface front passes 
to our east, sharply drier, refreshing air will return during the 
second part of the day.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Tranquil, seasonably warm conditions from late Sunday 
into Monday will prevail as a narrow axis of deep layer ridging
zips into and then out of our region to be replaced by a 
prefrontal trough Monday evening. Most of the impacts from this 
trough and the following cold front will follow Monday night, 
but overall the threat of showers and thunderstorms will ramp up
towards evening, particularly in northernmost portions of New 
York where both rain and thunder chances are highest through the
afternoon hours. Stronger storms currently look unlikely with 
only modest instability and shear, but we'll have to monitor any
trends in the data if they deviate from the current thinking.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A cold front is expected to cross the region Monday 
night, bringing an increased chance (45-85%) of precipitation to 
northern New York and Vermont, including some overnight embedded 
thunder. Temperatures will be on the milder side throughout the 
night, remaining at or above the mid 50s to mid 60s. Tuesday could 
also be a showery day with embedded thunder (precip chances 15-55%) 
under modest cold air advection and seasonable temperatures in the 
mid 70s to mid 80s. Mid week will feature a period of 15-55% chance 
of precipitation and seasonable temperatures (highs mid 70s to lower 
80s, lows 50s and lower 60s). Then, longwave troughing returns late 
week, bringing a resurgence of higher shower and thunderstorm 
chances on Thursday afternoon plus highs falling into the 70s for 
most both Thursday and Friday.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 00Z Sunday...Isolated to scattered showers will continue
through 08z Sat, mainly from KSLK eastward. VFR conditions
should prevail during that time, but brief reductions of both
visibility and ceilings to MVFR are possible with any
precipitation. Precipitation will exit after 08z, with perhaps
some partial clearing through early Saturday morning. Those
locations that receive rain this evening could see fog develop,
with the most likely timing 08z-12z. At this time, have the most
confidence in IFR conditions in fog at SLK/MPV, but it can't be
totally ruled out anywhere, though MSS has the lowest chances.
Otherwise, patchy MVFR ceilings/visibility in fog through 12z,
then conditions quickly improve to VFR for the remainder of the
day. Scattered showers and thunderstorms will redevelop after
16z, with MPV and EFK having the best chance of seeing
precipitation. Winds light and variable to calm overnight
tonight, trending toward S/SW 5-8 kt after 13z Sat.
